summary: Arithmetic Nielsen-core surfaces of area π times a minus continued-fraction period equidistribute by genus on the modular orbifold. The three-sign Hecke and half-weight trace identities connect surface integrals, geodesics and CM points. This 169-item checkpoint records pinned imports, owner-specific missing contracts, normalization corrections, a phase-uniqueness counterexample and eight explicit recursive source/proof gates; it does not certify complete closure. Continuation supplies the all-complex-parameter Appendix A proof and pins existing hypergeometric/gamma/integration suppliers; S1–S7 and residual S8 contracts remain open. Continuation codex-c83e7a: Biró author copy supplies the automorphic W∘U comparison, cusp Fourier adapter, finite-coefficient automorphy proof and positive-D normalization. Import built dual separation/Vitali/theta and planned j/GL₂ multiplicity. Repair the one-point convergence citation; retain boundary and nonvanishing gaps.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark after the proof of Proposition 1, p.968, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 184 (2016), 949–990 (publisher PDF, SHA-256 a67de715…5f61); the author preprint of 29 July 2016 on W. Duke's page has the same text there
sourceIssues.printed: "Remark. It is also possible to give an upper bound for ℓ_A. For example, Eichler [17] gave a general argument that yields for the modular group that ℓ_A < c log ε_D for an explicit c."
sourceIssues.correction: No bound ℓ_A ≪ log ε_D holds uniformly. ℓ_A can be about √D while log ε_D is about log D. Eichler's argument bounds the word length of the geometric code of the closed geodesic, which is a different quantity from ℓ_A.
sourceIssues.reason: Take a odd with a² + 4 squarefree, for example a = 13 or 101 (D = 173 or 10205 = 5·13·157). Then D = a² + 4 ≡ 5 (mod 8) is a fundamental discriminant, and a² + 4 is squarefree for a positive proportion of a. For the principal class, (a + √D)/2 has regular continued fraction [a; a, a, …]. A regular partial quotient a in an odd position becomes a run of a − 1 twos in the minus continued fraction, so the reduced period is ((a + 2, 2, …, 2)) with a − 1 twos, and ℓ_A = a. Meanwhile ε_D = ((a + √D)/2)² = (a² + 2 + a√D)/2, so log ε_D ≈ 2 log a, and ℓ_A / log ε_D → ∞. A direct computation for a = 5, 7, 13, 21, 51, 101, 201, 401 gives ℓ_A = a. In each case the product of the reduced w over the period equals ε_D, as in (6.3), which confirms that ℓ_A is the paper's quantity. The remark is not used elsewhere in the paper.
sourceIssues.known: Partly: P. Humphries and A. C. Nordentoft, "Sparse equidistribution of geometric invariants of real quadratic fields", arXiv 2211.05890v2 (28 August 2025), Remark 3.22, observe that Eichler's argument bounds the geometric code of the geodesic and not ℓ_A (the arithmetic code), so the remark is unsupported. They do not show that the bound fails. The counterexample family here is new.

sourceIssues.printed: "Weyl(⟨φ, φ⟩^{−1}φ, χ) ≪_ε r^C |D|^{13/28+ε}, (6.6) where … φ is any even Hecke–Maass cusp form with Laplace eigenvalue 1/4 + r²." Proof: "Part (6.6) of Proposition 2 follows straight from Theorem 4 and Theorem 5 of [12]."
sourceIssues.correction: State (6.6) for the unit vector u = φ/‖φ‖: Weyl(u, χ) ≪_ε r^C |D|^{13/28+ε}. It follows from Theorem 4 and [12, Theorem 5] together with the Rankin–Selberg size of ‖φ‖ for the normalization a(1) = 1. It is also what the proof of Theorem 2 uses, since c(φ)⟨φ, φ⟩^{−1}φ = ⟨f, u⟩u.
sourceIssues.reason: The forms φ are normalized by a(1) = 1 in (5.7), p.962, and the Shimura relation in Theorem 4 forces this too. [12, Theorem 5] (Duke 1988, p.85, read on the page image) bounds the coefficients of a spectral weight-1/2 form with eigenvalue 1/4 + t² by |λ|^A ch(πt/2)|n|^{−2/7+ε}. Here t = r/2, so Theorem 4 gives |Weyl(⟨φ, φ⟩^{−1}φ, χ)| ≪ r^C cosh²(πr/4)|D|^{3/4−2/7+ε}. That bound has an exponential factor, which (6.6) omits. The factor cannot simply be dropped. For a(1) = 1, Rankin–Selberg unfolding gives ⟨φ, φ⟩ ≍ L(1, sym²φ)/cosh(πr), so ⟨φ, φ⟩^{−1}φ is about e^{πr/2} times the unit vector u. As printed, (6.6) would therefore make the Weyl integrals of u exponentially small in r, which the cited results do not give. For u the two exponentials cancel: Weyl(u, χ) = ‖φ‖ Weyl(⟨φ, φ⟩^{−1}φ, χ) ≪ L(1, sym²φ)^{1/2} r^C |D|^{13/28+ε}, and L(1, sym²φ) ≪ r^ε. The coefficient bound "c(φ) ≪ |r|^{−A}" used for Theorem 2 on p.969 holds for u, so Theorem 2 stands. Noted by the extraction ("The spectral norm gate").
